Routing: Remix uses a file-based routing system in the app/routes directory. Each file represents a route segment, with dot and folder conventions creating nested URL structures automatically.
Nested Routes: Nested routes in Remix allow multiple components to render on the same URL. The parent route's layout wraps child routes through the <Outlet /> component, enabling complex UI hierarchies.
Layouts: Layout routes use the special app/root.tsx file and route-specific layout.tsx files. Layouts wrap child routes and persist across navigation, preventing full page re-renders.

loader: Loaders are server-side functions that fetch data before rendering a route. They run on every request, returning data that becomes available to the component via the useLoaderData hook.
useLoaderData: useLoaderData returns the typed data from the nearest route loader. It provides type safety when used with TypeScript and the typeof loader generic pattern.
params: Params give access to dynamic segments from the URL pattern. They are available in loaders and actions via the params argument, matching the bracket syntax in the route filename.

action: Actions handle form submissions and data mutations on the server. They run on POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE requests and can return data, redirects, or errors to the client.
Form: The <Form> component submits data without JavaScript by default. When JS loads, it progressively enhances to use fetch, providing optimistic UI and pending states without full page reloads.

import { Form } from '@remix-run/react';
<Form method='post'>
  <input name='title' />
  <button type='submit'>Create</button>
</Form>
useFetcher: useFetcher allows submitting actions or loading data without navigational transitions. It is ideal for non-blocking interactions like add-to-cart buttons or inline search suggestions.

const fetcher = useFetcher();
<fetcher.Form method='post' action='/api/cart'>
  <button type='submit'>Add to Cart</button>
</fetcher.Form>

Request/Response: Remix embraces Web Fetch API standards. Loaders and actions receive native Request objects and return Response objects, making routes portable across server environments.
Headers: Headers in Remix can be set at the route level for caching, security, and content negotiation. The headers export controls both document and resource route responses.
Cookies: Remix provides a cookies API that integrates with the Web Fetch standard. Cookies are created, read, and written using the cookie utilities from @remix-run/node.

ErrorBoundary: ErrorBoundary catches unexpected rendering errors in a route. When an error is thrown, Remix renders the closest ErrorBoundary instead of the default component, showing a fallback UI.
CatchBoundary: CatchBoundary handles expected error responses from loaders and actions. It receives the thrown Response object, allowing different UI for 404, 403, and other status codes.

Links: Remix manages CSS through the links export, which adds link tags to the document head. This enables route-level CSS loading and automatic cleanup when navigating away.
Route Styles: Route styles in Remix support both traditional CSS files and CSS-in-JS solutions. CSS files can be imported in links functions, with automatic scoping via CSS Modules.
Tailwind: Remix supports Tailwind CSS through the conventional PostCSS setup. The @tailwind directives are processed during build, generating optimized CSS with unused class purging.

Fly.io: Fly.io is the recommended deployment target for Remix, offering global edge regions and effortless scaling. Remix apps deploy as Docker containers running close to users worldwide.
Vercel: Vercel supports Remix via the @remix-run/vercel adapter. It automatically optimizes serverless functions and delivers assets through Vercel's edge network.
Netlify: Netlify deploys Remix apps using the Netlify adapter, providing serverless functions for the Remix server and global CDN for static assets via Netlify Edge.
Cloudflare: The Cloudflare Workers adapter runs Remix on Cloudflare's edge network. It uses Workers KV for sessions and Durable Objects for real-time state.

Resource Routes: Resource Routes return non-HTML content such as JSON, images, PDFs, or sitemaps. They handle requests without rendering a component, functioning as pure API endpoints within the routes system.
WebSockets: Real-time features in Remix are achieved through WebSocket integrations. While Remix does not include WebSockets natively, it pairs well with libraries like Socket.io or PartyKit.
Caching: Remix leverages HTTP caching extensively. The headers export allows setting Cache-Control headers per route, and loaders can implement conditional requests with ETags for efficient revalidation.
